newsitem.title: USA: Johnson Controls gets contract from Sears.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Controls gets contract from Sears.

text.p: Johnson Controls Inc, which was the sole supplier of DieHard batteries for Sears, Roebuck and Co until 1994, said Tuesday it will make a premium line of DieHard batteries for Sears beginning in October.
Under the three-year contract, Johnson Controls will manufacture DieHard Gold brand batteries for the retailer.

It is the second significant contract awarded to the company by Sears in the last year, the company said. Last June, Johnson Controls was named the sole supplier of "Tough One" automotive batteries to Western Auto and Part America stores, two auto retail outlets owned by Sears.
Johnson Controls was the sole supplier of the DieHard battery to Sears between 1967 and 1994, the company said.

Since 1994, Johnson Controls has transformed its battery business through improvements in quality and productivity which enabled it to reduce its number of manufacturing plants while increasing capacity, it said. The cost improvements, coupled with new proprietary battery technologies, have enabled the company to attract new customers and increase its North American market share, it added.
DieHard Gold batteries are sold in Sears Auto Centers, Sears Hardware and dealer stores, NTB National Tire & Battery stores, Sears Western Auto and Parts America stores, Johnson Controls said.
